rejected.title: The end of the White Australia policy
card: The White Australia policy, in place since 1901, used race to keep most non-European migrants out of Australia.
From 1966 the rules were eased, so some skilled non-European migrants could settle. In 1973 the Whitlam government ended the policy: race could no longer be used to choose migrants.
Multiculturalism followed. It is the idea that people of many backgrounds can keep their languages and customs while sharing in Australian life.
After the Vietnam War ended in 1975, thousands of refugees from Vietnam settled in Australia, some after arriving by boat.
rejected.remember: Race stopped deciding who could migrate, and Australia became more multicultural.

a.q: What changed when the White Australia policy ended in 1973?
opts: Race could no longer decide who was let in
Migration from Europe was stopped entirely
Migrants had to drop their own languages
Only skilled migrants could apply to settle
a.why: Ending the policy meant race could no longer be used to choose migrants. Letting in some skilled migrants describes the 1966 easing, when race still mattered, not the 1973 change.
a.clue: Think about what the policy had used to keep migrants out.

b.q: In 1979 a family from Vietnam settles in Darwin and opens a shop selling Vietnamese food. Which changes does their story reflect?
opts: The end of race-based entry, and multiculturalism
The 1966 easing only, as race still decided entry
Multiculturalism, but with race still deciding entry
The 1901 policy, which still chose migrants by race
b.why: The family could settle because race no longer decided entry, and keeping their food and customs fits multiculturalism. Before 1973 race still decided entry, even after the 1966 easing.
b.clue: Think about both why they could come and how they live.

version.title: The end of the White Australia policy
card: From 1901, the White Australia policy used race to keep most non-European migrants out of Australia.
From 1966 it was eased, so some skilled non-European migrants could settle. In 1973 the Whitlam government ended it: race could no longer be used to choose migrants.
Multiculturalism followed. It is the idea that people of many backgrounds can keep their own languages and customs while taking part in Australian life.
After the Vietnam War ended in 1975, tens of thousands of refugees from Vietnam settled in Australia. Some arrived by boat in northern Australia.
version.remember: From 1973 race no longer decided who could migrate, and multiculturalism grew.

a.q: How did the changes of 1966 differ from the end of the policy in 1973?
opts: 1966 eased the rules, and 1973 ended race as a test
1966 ended race as a test, and 1973 eased the rules
1966 eased the rules, and 1973 brought them back
1966 and 1973 both stopped all migration from Asia
a.why: From 1966 some skilled non-European migrants could settle, but race still counted. In 1973 the Whitlam government ended the policy, so race could no longer be used to choose migrants. The reversed order is the tempting mistake.

b.q: A Vietnamese family settles in Brisbane in 1980. They speak Vietnamese at home, celebrate Lunar New Year, and their children go to the local school. Which idea does this fit best?
opts: Multiculturalism, as they keep their culture
The White Australia policy, as race decided entry
The 1966 easing, as only skilled migrants came
Multiculturalism, as they give up their language
b.why: The family keeps its language and customs while taking part in Australian life, which is multiculturalism. Multiculturalism does not ask migrants to give up their language: keeping it is part of the idea.
b.clue: Do they keep their own language and customs?
